government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experimental Evidence From China
government.short_title: Social Norms, State Punishment, and Motivation Crowding in Anti‐Corruption Messaging: Experime…
government.source: Governance
government.plain_summary: This study examines how people's beliefs about corruption influence their attitudes towards fighting it. In a large survey experiment conducted in China, researchers found that when people were told the actual level of tolerance for corruption is much lower than they thought, it made them more likely to want to fight corruption. However, if this information was paired with suggestions of punishment, it seemed to weaken the effect. This shows that simply telling people about how corrupt others are might not be as effective as also showing what actions can be taken against it.

government.title: Institutional Legitimacy and Standard-Form Construction Contracts: Governance Lessons from NZS 3910
government.short_title: Institutional Legitimacy and Standard-Form Construction Contracts: Governance Lessons from NZS…
government.source: Journal of Legal Affairs and Dispute Resolution in Engineering and Construction
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how standard form construction contracts in New Zealand, like NZS 3910, influence how projects are managed and who makes decisions. These contracts are used by both private companies and the government. The research suggests that because the government both creates and frequently uses these contracts, there might be concerns about fairness and trust. The study also found that even when there are changes to how these contracts are used, the core issue of whether the government is properly overseeing the process remains.

government.title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Public Rights
government.short_title: An Examination of Government Methods for Compensating Damage Resulting from Infringement of Pu…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how governments in Iran handle situations where their actions harm collective interests or public rights. It examines legal systems that provide ways to compensate for such harms and restore balance. The research finds there are different types of compensation depending on whether the government acted wrongfully or not, and it also covers cases where they did something lawful but still caused damage. Challenges like unclear laws, difficulty proving harm in collective situations, and lack of coordination between different parts of the system can make these mechanisms less effective even if the basic rules are clear.

government.title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Official Channels: A Critical Analysis of the 2013 Anti‑Smuggling Law and Its 2021 Amendments
government.short_title: Evaluation of Iran's Legislative Criminal Policy on the Smuggling of Goods and Currency via Of…
government.source: Journal of Historical Research, Law and Policy
government.plain_summary: The smuggling of goods and currency through official channels in Iran remains a significant issue despite various laws enacted over the years. While there have been efforts like the 2013 Anti-Smuggling Law and subsequent amendments, this practice has not decreased but may have worsened in some areas such as reverse smuggling and organized currency trafficking. This article examines how well these laws balance different goals like prevention, repression, rehabilitation, and compensation. It found that while there are positive changes, the law still faces major issues including a broad definition of smuggling, multiple bodies leading to lengthy proceedings, disproportionate penalties, and weak enforcement due to corruption.

government.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
government.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
government.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
government.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

government.title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities of Nigeria
government.short_title: The treasury single account and fiscal transparency and accountability in federal universities…
government.source: RUDN Journal of Public Administration
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) was implemented in 2015 to centralize public funds and improve transparency and accountability in Nigerian federal universities, but financial irregularities still occur. This study found that TSA has improved transparency and accountability significantly (p=0.004), but also faces challenges like bureaucratic delays and actors circumventing the system. Corruption persists as it transforms into less traceable forms. Despite savings of over 10 trillion Naira nationally, corruption perception scores remain low.

government.title: Citizens' perceptions of accountability in AI-based public sector decision making
government.short_title: Citizens' perceptions of accountability in AI-based public sector decision making
government.source: Government Information Quarterly

government.title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-based analysis
government.short_title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-ba…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how ready Tanzania's public sector is for better connecting its different government departments and services. They found that strong support from government leaders and clear plans are very important. Also, having good technology like computers and internet is crucial. But the biggest challenge is having enough money to keep these systems running and improving them.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.short_title: A Policy Analysis of PFAS Regulations in Maine and the US Federal Government
government.source: Maine Policy Review
government.plain_summary: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are harmful chemicals found in many products that have contaminated the environment. The US government has not uniformly addressed PFAS issues, but some states like Maine have taken strong actions. Maine has implemented various measures such as education, labeling requirements, and bans on certain agricultural practices. They also have unique regulations like banning the use of PFAS in food products like beef, dairy, and eggs.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.source: International Journal of Government Auditing
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Technology is Advancing Every Day, We Think Oversight Should Too!
government.short_title: Technology is Advancing Every Day, We Think Oversight Should Too!
government.source: International Journal of Government Auditing

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.source: International Journal of Government Auditing
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.source: Gestion et management public
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Market Failure or Government Failure? A Response to Jaworski
government.short_title: Market Failure or Government Failure? A Response to Jaworski
government.source: Business Ethics Journal Review

government.title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representative cross-sectional study
government.short_title: Anti-HBc seropositivity among women of childbearing age in Indonesia: a nationally representat…
government.source: Frontiers in Public Health
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how many Indonesian women aged 15 to 49 have been exposed to the hepatitis B virus. It found that women over 35 years old, those with less education, who work, live in rural areas, or use birth control are more likely to have this exposure. The main finding is that many women in this age group are still at risk for hepatitis B. This means healthcare providers should pay extra attention to these women, offering them tests, vaccines, and other preventive measures.

government.title: Government Transparency Increases Trust in Government: Disentangling Effects of Government Transparency From Effects of Information
government.short_title: Government Transparency Increases Trust in Government: Disentangling Effects of Government Tra…
government.source: Public Administration Quarterly
government.plain_summary: The study found that government transparency generally increases trust in government, but this relationship can be explained by different theories. Government transparency can make people trust the government more, which aligns with the idea that government acts help citizens understand and participate in decision-making (deliberative democracy theory). However, it also shows that the information disclosed can either increase or decrease trust, depending on how the information is presented. This means that when the government discloses information, it can either build or break trust, not just because of the transparency itself but also because of the information provided.

government.title: Lobbying Regulation, Anti-Corruption, and the Fight Against Foreign Influence in the European Union after Qatargate: Coherent Approach or Double Standards?
government.short_title: Lobbying Regulation, Anti-Corruption, and the Fight Against Foreign Influence in the European…
government.source: European Journal of Risk Regulation
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how the European Union handles anti-corruption measures and lobbying rules. Since 2020, the EU has mentioned lobbying rules in their reports on anti-corruption efforts, focusing on what countries within the EU are doing. However, after a major scandal involving foreign influence and corruption, the EU has been pushing for reforms to protect itself from such issues. The article discusses these recent developments and how they relate to the EU's overall anti-corruption and lobbying policies.

government.title: Governing artificial intelligence in public services: accountability, transparency and democratic AI governance
government.short_title: Governing artificial intelligence in public services: accountability, transparency and democra…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how democratic governments can manage artificial intelligence in public services by creating frameworks that are transparent, accountable, and governable. It proposes a framework called TAG, which stands for Transparent, Accountable, and Governable. The TAG Framework combines elements like transparency, accountability, and governance to ensure AI is used ethically and responsibly. Practically, this means things like public registers of AI systems, assessing the impact of algorithms, having human oversight, and regular audits.

government.title: LAWYERS AS GATE-KEEPERS IN ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING REGULATIONS IN NIGERIA
government.short_title: LAWYERS AS GATE-KEEPERS IN ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING REGULATIONS IN NIGERIA
government.source: Journal of Human, Social and Political Science Research
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant financial crime that harms economies and governments. Lawyers play a crucial role in corporate and financial transactions, acting as gatekeepers to prevent or facilitate such activities. The paper discusses how lawyers are now seen as important in anti-money laundering (AML) regulations. It highlights the need for lawyers to balance their duty of confidentiality with the requirement to report suspicious activities.

government.title: From Soft-Law AI Ethics to Risk-Based Public Sector AI Procurement: Recalibrating Malaysia’s Post-PDPA Governance Model
government.short_title: From Soft-Law AI Ethics to Risk-Based Public Sector AI Procurement: Recalibrating Malaysia’s P…
government.source: LAW & PASS: International Journal of Law, Public Administration and Social Studies
government.plain_summary: In recent years, governments have started acquiring AI systems through procurement rather than developing them in-house. This change means that instead of just ensuring ethical principles are followed, governments need to make those principles enforceable throughout the AI system's lifecycle. In Malaysia, they have introduced guidelines for AI governance and procurement. However, simply having privacy compliance and ethical principles isn't enough to manage AI in public administration.

government.title: X Use and Policy Contestation: Examining Public Demands for Government Accountability During Kenya’s 2024 Finance Bill Protests in Nairobi
government.short_title: X Use and Policy Contestation: Examining Public Demands for Government Accountability During K…
government.source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCE HUMANITY & MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study examines how people used social media platforms like X to protest the 2024 Kenya Finance Bill in Nairobi. They used various posts and hashtags to demand government accountability, focusing on issues like taxes affecting household welfare and the legitimacy of government decisions. Protesters also called for accountability from elected officials and protection of their rights. The research found that different types of accounts used social media in different ways—activists and public figures focused on advocacy and mobilization, while media accounts shared official statements.

government.title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
government.short_title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how Nigeria's public sector handles whistleblowing and anti-corruption efforts from 2015 to 2024. It found that while the policy helped recover some public funds, it faced many challenges like weak laws, lack of protection for whistleblowers, and poor coordination among agencies. Many whistleblowers faced retaliation, which discouraged them from coming forward. The study suggests making stronger laws, improving how agencies work together, and educating the public more to make the policy more effective.

government.title: Network Governance for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Partnerships to Implement UN SDGs in Anti‐Desertification Projects
government.short_title: Network Governance for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Partnerships to Implement UN SDGs in…
government.source: Public Administration and Development
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups can work together more effectively to fight desertification and restore land, which is part of the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. It found that simply telling people what to do isn't as effective as involving everyone and thinking about how systems work together. By doing this, they can get more people involved and keep working together even when things get complicated. This is important for countries trying to improve their environment and meet these goals.

government.title: The Wheel of Corruption as a Vehicle for Development? Global Debates, African Realities, And a Reappraisal of the Abacha Loot
government.short_title: The Wheel of Corruption as a Vehicle for Development? Global Debates, African Realities, And a…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: The debate on corruption as a development tool has been revived in global discussions. Some argue that illicit wealth can be used for development if properly managed. This article looks at this idea from a global and African perspective, focusing on Nigeria's Abacha-loot case. It found that while recovering assets can bring some benefits, corruption often leads to new forms of rent-seeking.

government.title: The hidden mental health burden of corruption in healthcare: Findings from a scoping review and key informant interviews
government.short_title: The hidden mental health burden of corruption in healthcare: Findings from a scoping review an…
government.source: PLOS Global Public Health
government.plain_summary: Corruption in healthcare can cause significant mental health issues for patients, healthcare providers, and those fighting corruption. It leads to stress, anxiety, and depression. It also damages trust in healthcare systems and can normalize unethical behavior. To address this, policies should focus on protecting whistleblowers, strengthening reporting systems, and adapting anti-corruption measures to local conditions.

government.short_title: Does Corruption Erode Institutional Trust? Micro-level Evidence from Sub-Saharan Africa”

government.source: GLOBAL BUSINESS FINANCE REVIEW

government.title: The Impact of Poor Records Management Practices on Service Delivery and Accountability in Local Government Councils (LGCs) in Oyo State, Nigeria
government.short_title: The Impact of Poor Records Management Practices on Service Delivery and Accountability in Loca…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study found that local government councils in Oyo State, Nigeria often use outdated paper-based systems for managing records. This leads to delays in service delivery and increased fees for expedited services. It also makes it harder to track who is responsible for what, which can lead to misuse of power. To improve, councils need to digitize their records, train staff on modern record management, and strengthen accountability measures.

government.title: Treasury Single Account (TSA), Accountability and Transparency in Public Finance Management in Nigeria
government.short_title: Treasury Single Account (TSA), Accountability and Transparency in Public Finance Management in…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: The Treasury Single Account (TSA) has improved accountability and transparency in managing public finance in Nigeria, according to a study. The research found that TSA significantly affects how well public finance is handled. This means TSA is working well in ensuring that public money is used properly and openly. The study suggests that the government should continue to provide training for those who use TSA to make sure it works effectively.

government.title: Accountability and Good Governance in Local Government Administration: A Study of Obio/Akpor, Andoni, and Ahoada West in Rivers State, 2014–2024
government.short_title: Accountability and Good Governance in Local Government Administration: A Study of Obio/Akpor,…
government.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how well local governments in three areas of Rivers State, Nigeria, are doing in terms of being accountable and providing good services. It found that when governments effectively manage resources, include everyone in decision-making, have regular public meetings, and improve health services, they are doing a good job. However, problems like weak structures, corruption, and interference from higher levels of government can hurt their performance. The study suggests ways to improve accountability and inclusiveness, like making budgets transparent, involving citizens more, and working together with other institutions.

government.title: An Assessment of EFCC Anti-Corruption Agency in Nigeria, 2015- 2025
government.short_title: An Assessment of EFCC Anti-Corruption Agency in Nigeria, 2015- 2025
government.source: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how the EFCC, Nigeria's anti-corruption agency, has worked from 2015 to 2018. It found that the EFCC is often used by different governments to target their opponents. To improve, the study suggests that governments should make sure there are no ways to misuse their positions. It also recommends reducing centralization of power and ensuring that people get their salaries and allowances on time.

government.title: Artificial Intelligence and Anti-Corruption: A Theoretical Framework of Detection, Deterrence and Displacement in Public Procurement and Fiscal Oversight
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence and Anti-Corruption: A Theoretical Framework of Detection, Deterrence…

government.short_title: Threshold associations between governance integrity and public satisfaction with government he…
government.source: Health Economics Review

government.title: Public Sector Corruption and Accountability in Anambra State Ministry of Education, 2015–2025
government.short_title: Public Sector Corruption and Accountability in Anambra State Ministry of Education, 2015–2025
government.source: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study looked at corruption and accountability issues in the Anambra State Ministry of Education from 2015 to 2025. It found that misuse of funds and favoritism were major problems. Misuse of funds included things like inflated contracts, incomplete deliveries, and discrepancies between what was planned and what was actually done. Favoritism meant that people with connections got more benefits.

government.title: “Nobody Wants a Trailer That Had Dead Bodies in It”: A Descriptive Study of the Ethics of Public Sector Deathcare
government.short_title: “Nobody Wants a Trailer That Had Dead Bodies in It”: A Descriptive Study of the Ethics of Publ…
government.source: Public Administration Quarterly
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public sector deathcare workers, like medical examiners and coroners, handle their roles. Despite being guided by science and rules, they often face tough decisions influenced by empathy, politics, and resource limitations. The research shows that ethical leadership is crucial, but they also use neutral competence and professional standards. Personal conduct is key to maintaining accountability in these challenging situations.

government.title: Public Procurement Policy Compliance, Corruption Risk, and Value-for-Money in Ghana's Infrastructure Sector: An Institutional Analysis
government.short_title: Public Procurement Policy Compliance, Corruption Risk, and Value-for-Money in Ghana's Infrastr…
government.source: International Journal of Public Policy and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how following or not following rules when buying things for public projects in Ghana affects corruption and how much value those projects provide. It found that not following the rules, especially in areas like choosing bidders fairly, keeping proper records, and checking on projects after they start, leads to more corruption and less value for money. Stronger oversight and better training for people who handle these projects can help reduce corruption. The research helps policymakers understand what works best to stop corruption in Ghana's infrastructure projects.

government.title: Not All Protections are Equal: A Review of U.S. Anti-Bullying Laws
government.short_title: Not All Protections are Equal: A Review of U.S. Anti-Bullying Laws
government.source: Journal of Disability Policy Studies
government.plain_summary: Bullying is a common issue in schools, but there isn't a federal law that directly addresses it. States are responsible for creating their own laws and policies about bullying. While many states now have definitions of bullying, there are still big gaps in how they handle issues like power imbalances, repeated bullying, and bullying based on someone's identity. These differences mean some students might not get the same level of protection depending on where they go to school.

government.title: DIGITAL FORENSIC ACCOUNTING: INTEGRATING DIGITAL EVIDENCE, ADVANCED ANALYTICS AND PROFESSIONAL JUDGEMENT FOR FRAUD DETECTION AND FINANCIAL INTEGRITY
government.short_title: DIGITAL FORENSIC ACCOUNTING: INTEGRATING DIGITAL EVIDENCE, ADVANCED ANALYTICS AND PROFESSIONAL…
government.source: International Journal of Management, Public Policy and Research
government.plain_summary: Digital forensic accounting is becoming crucial as financial systems increasingly rely on digital technology. This field combines accounting knowledge with investigative methods, digital forensics, and advanced technologies to detect fraud and maintain financial integrity. Tools like digital evidence, data analytics, AI, and machine learning can help identify suspicious transactions and examine financial data. However, there are challenges such as technological complexity, privacy concerns, legal and ethical issues, and the need for specialized skills.

government.title: Nigerian Public Sector Governance and Fiscal Transparency: Empirical Data from Kwara State.
government.short_title: Nigerian Public Sector Governance and Fiscal Transparency: Empirical Data from Kwara State.
government.source: JOURNAL OF POLITICAL SCIENCE AND LEADERSHIP RESEARCH
government.plain_summary: This study focuses on Nigerian public sector governance and fiscal transparency in Kwara State. It found that involving all citizens in planning processes helps protect the environment, expand economic opportunities, and meet social needs. The research also highlighted that fiscal transparency is crucial for good governance in Kwara State. The study recommends that the state government should involve citizens in budget processes and invest more in agriculture.

government.title: Cybersecurity Strategy and Spoofing Outcomes in Public Corporate Finance in the United States of America
government.short_title: Cybersecurity Strategy and Spoofing Outcomes in Public Corporate Finance in the United States…
government.source: Journal of Leadership, Accountability and Ethics
government.plain_summary: Spoofing attacks misuse trusted digital identities to cause financial fraud and operational disruptions. This study found that higher levels of information security maturity and better cybersecurity strategies were linked to fewer spoofing incidents and less financial loss. The stronger the maturity and strategy, the fewer spoofing events and financial losses an organization reported. For cybersecurity providers and public buyers, these findings suggest pairing technical controls with verified organizational readiness and outcomes is valuable.

government.title: Building Integrity in the Global South: Lessons from Pakistan’s Struggle Against Public Sector Corruption
government.short_title: Building Integrity in the Global South: Lessons from Pakistan’s Struggle Against Public Sector…
government.source: International Journal of Public Administration

government.title: Corruption pathways and governance failures in Thailand’s public construction projects: Phases, mechanisms, and stakeholders
government.short_title: Corruption pathways and governance failures in Thailand’s public construction projects: Phases…
government.source: Journal of Governance and Regulation
government.plain_summary: This study examines corruption in Thailand's public construction projects, looking at seven main ways corruption happens across all phases of a project. It found that corruption is most common during the planning, bidding, and execution stages. The study also shows that corruption is supported by interactions among government officials, contractors, and other stakeholders. It suggests that to prevent corruption, it's important to address issues like government transparency, fair bidding processes, and better oversight.

government.title: Reengineering trust: E-public procurement and government transparency
government.short_title: Reengineering trust: E-public procurement and government transparency
government.source: Journal of Governance and Regulation
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how e-procurement, which is using digital technology for buying goods and services, can help make government buying more fair, transparent, and honest. It shows that e-procurement can reduce opportunities for corruption by limiting direct contact between officials and contractors. However, it also points out that there are challenges like not having enough technology or support from institutions. The main idea is that while e-procurement is important, it needs to be supported by fixing these issues to work well.

government.title: Corruption and public healthcare quality in the European Union: Evidence from Europe’s regions
government.short_title: Corruption and public healthcare quality in the European Union: Evidence from Europe’s regions
government.source: Health Policy

government.title: Ownership and efficiency in municipal waste management: evidence from a fragmented local government system
government.short_title: Ownership and efficiency in municipal waste management: evidence from a fragmented local gover…
government.source: International Journal of Public Sector Management
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the ownership of waste collection providers affects the efficiency of municipal waste management in Croatia. It uses a two-stage analysis, first looking at cost and environmental service efficiency, and then examining the relationship between ownership types and these efficiencies while controlling for other factors. The findings suggest that having internal ownership, where the municipality owns the waste collection company, is not associated with efficiency. However, mixed ownership, where the municipality and other public entities share ownership, is negatively related to cost efficiency.

government.title: COUNTERING CORRUPTION IN PUBLIC PROCUREMENT: CRIMINAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE LAW ASPECTS
government.short_title: COUNTERING CORRUPTION IN PUBLIC PROCUREMENT: CRIMINAL AND ADMINISTRATIVE LAW ASPECTS

government.title: Digital transformation in e-government services: exploring the role of public trust, transparency, accountability and citizen satisfaction in real-time service delivery
government.short_title: Digital transformation in e-government services: exploring the role of public trust, transpare…
government.source: Journal of Science and Technology Policy Management
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how e-government services can be improved by making them more transparent, accountable, and trusted. It found that when people believe the government is open and honest about what it does, and that it follows rules fairly, they are more likely to use these services. The study also shows that if people feel their efforts are worth it and that the service helps them, they are more likely to use it. This research helps governments create better e-government services by making them more transparent and accountable, which in turn makes people more willing to use them.

government.title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector digital development
government.short_title: How digital portfolios become governable: a venture design research study of public sector dig…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study explores how public sector organizations can better govern digital development projects. It suggests that instead of relying on existing tools, digital solutions should be designed to make governance more visible, comparable, and subject to collective decision-making. The research found that by actively specifying governance through design, digital solutions can lead to more transparent discussions and decisions. However, long-term outcomes like strategic alignment and public value creation are harder to measure.

government.title: Responsible AI beyond compliance: governing everyday use in the public sector
government.short_title: Responsible AI beyond compliance: governing everyday use in the public sector
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public sector organizations manage the use of AI, focusing on how they align everyday practices with governance and accountability requirements. Despite formal structures, employees often use AI in ways that don't align with these structures, leading to a governance-practice gap. To address this, governance evolves through various mechanisms like technical controls, human oversight, and informal guidance. The findings suggest that AI use doesn't replace human judgement but rather intensifies it, requiring more verification and training.

government.title: Systemic Imbalances in Integrity Management Systems: A Meso‐Level Framework From Four Corruption Scandals
government.short_title: Systemic Imbalances in Integrity Management Systems: A Meso‐Level Framework From Four Corrupti…
government.source: Regulation & Governance
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses how integrity management systems (IMSs) are used to promote ethical conduct and prevent corruption. Despite their promotion, there's little understanding of how these systems work in practice. The study developed a framework that looks at four key areas: belief, boundary, diagnostic, and interaction systems of control. It analyzed four major corruption cases in different sectors like infrastructure, healthcare, banking, and defense.

government.title: Transparent budget: the idea of deep transparency
government.short_title: Transparent budget: the idea of deep transparency
government.source: Public Sector Economics
government.plain_summary: Transparent budgeting means governments know exactly where public money goes, but citizens often don't. This paper suggests a new way to make spending transparent so citizens can see every penny goes to the right person. It uses special technology like WORM storage and blockchain to connect where money is allocated to where it's actually spent. This makes it harder for people to misuse public funds, like giving favors or stealing money.

government.title: Strategic Planning Practices and Accountability for Accomplishment in Ethiopian Public Sector: Trajectory Probing
government.short_title: Strategic Planning Practices and Accountability for Accomplishment in Ethiopian Public Sector:…
government.source: PanAfrican Journal of Governance and Development (PJGD)
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how Ethiopian public sector organizations prepare and implement strategic plans, and how they hold themselves accountable for achieving their goals. It found that while the overall level of strategic planning is moderate, the implementation and evaluation parts are weaker. The main factors affecting the success of these plans are organizational culture, leadership, and communication. The study suggests that improving accountability and providing necessary resources are key for successful strategic planning.

government.title: Working Paper 63: Anticipating future corruption
government.short_title: Working Paper 63: Anticipating future corruption
government.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
government.plain_summary: This working paper from the Basel Institute on Governance discusses how understanding corruption in complex systems can help improve anti-corruption efforts. It introduces foresight and anticipatory governance approaches to anticipate potential issues and opportunities before they happen, making strategies more effective against corruption. Practitioners can use these insights to develop proactive plans that are less reactive and better equipped to handle future challenges.

government.title: Legal Corruption in the Government: An Experimental Study on the Role of Civil Servants' Political Ideology
government.short_title: Legal Corruption in the Government: An Experimental Study on the Role of Civil Servants' Polit…
government.source: Regulation & Governance
government.plain_summary: This research examines how civil servants view government legal corruption using a survey experiment involving over 2000 South Korean civil servants. It found that their judgment of legal corruption is influenced by their own political ideology. Civil servants are more critical when the government they work for has different political views from theirs, compared to when it aligns with them. This study highlights how political beliefs shape perceptions of corruption within public institutions, suggesting that understanding these ideological differences can help in addressing and preventing corruption effectively.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATION
nonprofit.short_title: THE CYBERNETIC DIAGNOSTIC OF ANTI-NARCOTIC SYSTEM: MODEL RAS-VI AS A TOOL OF SYSTEMIC EVALUATI…
nonprofit.source: Problems of Social Hygiene, Public Health and History of Medicine
nonprofit.plain_summary: The study proposes a cybernetic diagnostic tool called RAS-VI (Resilience-Adaptability-Synergy-Diversity Index) for evaluating the effectiveness of anti-narcotics policies at different levels. This model uses principles from cybernetics and systems theory to assess how well regional anti-narcotics systems can adapt, work together, and maintain stability. Key indicators like resilience, adaptability, synergy, and diversity are used to measure these aspects. By applying RAS-VI, policymakers can better understand the strengths and weaknesses of their system and improve its overall effectiveness in managing drug issues.

nonprofit.title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-based analysis
nonprofit.short_title: Institutional readiness for business process integration in Tanzania’s public sector: a TOE-ba…
nonprofit.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how ready Tanzania's public sector is for better connecting its different government departments and services. They found that strong support from government leaders and clear plans are very important. Also, having good technology like computers and internet is crucial. But the biggest challenge is having enough money to keep these systems running and improving them.

nonprofit.title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
nonprofit.short_title: Whistleblowing Policy and Anti-Corruption Effort in Nigeria's Public Sector, 2015-2024
nonprofit.source: JOURNAL OF PUBLIC ADMINISTRATION AND SOCIAL WELFARE RESEARCH
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how Nigeria's public sector handles whistleblowing and anti-corruption efforts from 2015 to 2024. It found that while the policy helped recover some public funds, it faced many challenges like weak laws, lack of protection for whistleblowers, and poor coordination among agencies. Many whistleblowers faced retaliation, which discouraged them from coming forward. The study suggests making stronger laws, improving how agencies work together, and educating the public more to make the policy more effective.

nonprofit.title: Governing Lawful Basis Selection in the Saudi Third Sector: Nonprofit Accountability under the Personal Data Protection Law
nonprofit.short_title: Governing Lawful Basis Selection in the Saudi Third Sector: Nonprofit Accountability under the…
nonprofit.source: Voluntas: International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
nonprofit.plain_summary: This article discusses how nonprofit organizations in Saudi Arabia can better manage data use by choosing the right legal basis for their data practices. Often, this is seen as just a legal requirement, but the article suggests it's also a way to hold the board accountable. By carefully selecting the legal basis, the board can ensure that the organization is transparent about its data uses and considers the risks to different stakeholders. This helps in making sure the organization is acting in a way that aligns with its mission and values.

nonprofit.title: The Accountability Architecture: Linking Robust Financial Controls to Institutional Advancement in the NGO Sector
nonprofit.short_title: The Accountability Architecture: Linking Robust Financial Controls to Institutional Advancemen…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at how strong financial controls affect the growth of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in East Africa. It found that having good financial controls, especially strong internal systems, helps NGOs grow. The research used surveys and interviews to gather data. The key takeaway is that NGOs need to focus on their financial controls to grow and be successful.
